security.reviewer: Independent general-purpose review agent, adversarial brief; traced depthOf's invariant against the schema's actual node/issue shape rather than accepting the task description's framing, checked every one of the fourteen flat-collection FKs against prisma/schema.prisma for an undisclosed intra-collection dependency, and read the actual RLS migration SQL to confirm per-row policy enforcement under a multi-row INSERT.

findings.summary: A createMany failure on a dangling foreign key surfaces one generic constraint error for the whole batch rather than naming the offending row.
findings.disposition: accepted -- both forms roll back to the same end state inside the one transaction; marginal debuggability cost only

findings.summary: A single createMany statement is capped by Postgres at 65,535 bind parameters; an unusually large same-depth batch (roughly 1,800+ issues) would approach it, a failure mode the old per-row loop never had.
findings.disposition: accepted -- unexercised headroom at this codebase's current stated scale of hundreds of rows per tenant, tracked as a forward-looking limit

conditions: F1 and F2 (both LOW) stay open as recorded, tracked risks -- neither blocks merge, per this house's own gate (fail or a HIGH/MEDIUM finding stops for review; LOW-only findings on a pass do not).

Four items from the same industry-standard review remain open: the missing HierarchyNode.sowId index (LOW, needs a Prisma migration and architect approval), the HIGH migration expand/contract policy decision (a documentation/process change, not a code fix), and the remaining frontend findings in components/IssueWorkspace.tsx (owner-assignment override visibility, the blocking native confirm(), the search-flash effect, the mirrorError double-effect) -- tracked, not part of this correction's scope.
